meta.name: Moderate WhatsApp groups, block link spam, and auto-welcome members with Wafly

name: Protect WhatsApp groups from link spam with strikes and auto-removal

parameters.content:
[![Workflow overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iagovelasco3/n8n-nodes-wafly/main/assets/template-previews/05-moderate-whatsapp-group.png)](https://wafly.io/signup?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=workflow_template&utm_campaign=group_moderation&utm_content=workflow_preview)

## Protect WhatsApp groups with deduplication, allowlists and repeat-offender strikes

> **Community node - self-hosted n8n only.** This template uses `n8n-nodes-wafly`, which cannot be installed on n8n Cloud.

### Who's it for

Paid communities, customer groups and class cohorts where admins need more than a one-rule link filter. The workflow is designed for noisy webhook delivery and applies the same policy consistently across join requests, welcome events and group messages.

### What makes it production-oriented

- Rejects malformed events and suppresses webhook retries for a configurable window.
- Normalizes phone numbers and domains before comparing them.
- Exempts admins and exact or subdomain matches from moderation.
- Deletes disallowed links, explains the action and records time-bounded strikes.
- Can remove repeat offenders after a configurable threshold; escalation is disabled by default for safety.
- Keeps every policy value in one Config node.

### Safety model

Start with `removeRepeatOffenders = false`. Verify the allowlist and admin list with real group events, inspect n8n executions, and only then enable automatic removal. Duplicate suppression and strikes use workflow static data, so test them with an active workflow rather than manual executions.

### Requirements

Self-hosted n8n, `n8n-nodes-wafly` 1.5.5+, a Wafly account, and the connected number promoted to group admin.

## Setup and rollout

1. Create a **Wafly API** credential (Client-Token, instance, token). The connected number must be a **group admin**.
2. In **Config**, replace the example admin phones and domains. Keep country codes and omit `+`.
3. Choose the policy:
   - `duplicateWindowSeconds`: ignores repeated webhook deliveries.
   - `strikeWindowMinutes`: how long a strike remains active.
   - `strikeLimit`: threshold for escalation.
   - `removeRepeatOffenders`: keep `false` during validation; set `true` only after checking executions.
4. Activate the workflow, copy the Webhook **Production URL** and register it once:

```
curl -X PUT \
  "https://wafly.com.br/api-bridge-whats/instances/YOUR_INSTANCE/token/YOUR_TOKEN/update-webhook-received" \
  -H "Client-Token: YOUR_CLIENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value":"PASTE_THE_PRODUCTION_URL"}'
```

### Test plan

Send an allowed link as a member, a blocked link as an admin, then a blocked link as a normal member. Replay the last payload to confirm deduplication. Finally lower `strikeLimit` in a test group and enable removal to validate escalation.

Events used:
- `MEMBERSHIP_APPROVAL_REQUEST` -> approve pending member
- `GROUP_PARTICIPANT_INVITE` -> welcome new member
- group message with text -> evaluate links and policy
